chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ibn Faddal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah, who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who divorces his wife. He said: 'She inherits him and he inherits her as long as he has the right of return (raj'ah) over her.'

key_terms.تَرِثُهُ وَ يَرِثُهَا: She inherits him and he inherits her; indicating mutual inheritance rights.
key_terms.رَجْعَةٌ: Right of return; the husband's right to take back his wife during the revocable divorce waiting period.
key_terms.يُطَلِّقُ: He divorces; specifically referring to revocable divorce in this context.

ai.seo_question: Do divorced spouses inherit from each other during the waiting period?
ai.summary: Reported by Zurarah, a prominent companion of Imam al-Baqir, this hadith clarifies that in a revocable divorce (taliq raj'i), the marital bond remains intact during the iddah, thereby preserving mutual inheritance rights. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that the legal effects of marriage persist until the iddah concludes or the divorce becomes irrevocable, distinguishing it from the final divorce where inheritance ceases immediately.
